# Helping your midwife find you

*A page from the Riverside Community Midwives welcome pack*

## Hello from your midwives

We know you have a lot on your mind before your baby arrives. This page is about one small job that makes a big difference: helping us find your front door quickly when it is time.

We are not going to tell you off about anything. We have been lost on your street before, and we will be again. Honest mistakes happen to all of us. What helps is a bit of planning, and this page will show you how.

## When can we come to your home?

Our home birth cover starts from **37 weeks**. If your baby is coming before then, you will need to go to the hospital. We tell everyone this at your booking visit, but we know it can slip out of your head, so please check with us if you are not sure.

## When labour starts: phone the birth line

When labour starts, please **phone the Riverside birth line on [Riverside birth line number]**.

Please do not call a midwife's personal mobile. The birth line goes to whichever midwife is on call that night, so the right person always gets your call, even if your usual midwife is off duty.

If something does not feel right at any point, call the birth line straight away. In an emergency, call **999**.

## Two midwives, two cars, and a lot of stuff

For the birth, two midwives usually come. We often arrive in separate cars, so **two parking spaces near your house would be a huge help** if you can keep them free.

We carry a lot of equipment. That can include gas and air cylinders, the big bag, and sometimes a birthing pool and its bits. Our arms get tired. If you can, leave a clear path from the car to the door, and please do not leave bins or bikes in the way.

## Parking and permits

Some of our families live in areas with permit parking, including around Anfield and Kensington. You have two options:

- **Ask the council for a visitor permit** before your due date, so it is ready when you need it.
- **Leave a visitor permit on your dashboard** when we arrive, if you have one.

Please check the council's website or call them to find out how to get a visitor permit for your street. We have had tickets before, and nobody wants that at 3am.

## Finding your front door

Please think about how we will find you in the dark. Late at night, dark streets can all look the same.

**Put your full address on paper.** Include your house number, flat number, street name, and postcode. A house name on its own is not enough. One of our midwives once drove to "Rosemary Cottage" in a street full of terraced houses, and the sat nav took her to the chip shop. Lovely chips, but not the birth.

**Flats need extra care.** If you live in a block of flats, write the block name, the entrance, and the flat number. Please check that flat 14 is in the building you think it is. One midwife drove round a block in Everton for 20 minutes, and in the end the dad was waving a tea towel out of the window to guide her in. Please do not make us do that.

**Send us your location.** A what3words address is very useful. You can also send a map pin on WhatsApp to the birth line phone. Please test it before your due date so you know it works.

**Put your porch light on at night.** This is one of the easiest things you can do. A light on your front door helps us spot the house straight away.

**Balloons on the gate are a brilliant idea.** One family put balloons on their gate like it was a party, and we found them straight away. You do not need to go that far, but anything bright and easy to see helps.

**If you have a rough idea of where you live, tell us.** Things like "the house with the blue door next to the corner shop" are very helpful.

## When we arrive

**Pets:** We love dogs, honestly. But please keep your pets in another room while we are working, especially during the pushing stage. One very friendly staffie called Pippin jumped on a midwife at every visit, and she nearly dropped the gas and air. Pippin is lovely, but it is safer for everyone if pets are shut away.

**Space:** Please clear the stairs and the hallway so we can get through with our bags. Put away washing baskets, toys, and anything that might trip someone up. Lego is the enemy of midwives everywhere.

**Shoes:** Please ask visitors to leave their shoes at the door. We will do the same and wear our own shoe covers.

**Other things to do before we come:**
- Have a clear, warm room ready for the birth
- Keep a torch handy for the walk to the door
- Make sure someone is awake and ready to let us in

## Our promise to you

We are coming to your home to help you, as a friend. Where I was raised in the Philippines, we say the midwife is like family. We hope you will feel that when we arrive. You do not need to be perfect, and you do not need a tidy house. You just need a clear route to the door, a bit of light, and a phone ready to call the birth line.

We will do the rest.

## Fridge checklist

Tick these off and stick the page on your fridge.

- [ ] I know I should call the birth line when labour starts, not a midwife's personal phone
- [ ] I have the birth line number saved in my phone and written on the fridge: [Riverside birth line number]
- [ ] My baby is due after 37 weeks, or I know to go to hospital if labour starts earlier
- [ ] I have my full address written down, with the house number, flat number, and postcode
- [ ] I have sent my what3words address or map pin to the birth line phone
- [ ] I have checked that flat numbers and house names match the building
- [ ] I have a visitor permit, or I know how to get one from the council
- [ ] I have kept two parking spaces free if I can
- [ ] My porch light works, and I know how to switch it on
- [ ] Pets are sorted and can be shut away during the birth
- [ ] Stairs and hallway are clear, with no shoes, washing baskets, or Lego in the way
- [ ] I have a torch by the door
- [ ] Someone in the house knows how to let the midwives in
- [ ] I know to call 999 in an emergency

---

*Riverside Community Midwives. If you have any questions about this page, please ask your midwife at your next visit.*

---

Before this goes out, you'll want to fill in the [Riverside birth line number] placeholders and check two things with Deb: the 37-week cover rule and the current council permit process for Anfield and Kensington, since those can change. Let me know if you want it shorter for the Facebook group or a version with a bit less of the personal stories.
